topics.sampleQuestion: How do I design a share loop so my app grows without paid ads?

topics.summary: Ship an ugly v1 quickly, iterate with small measured tweaks, and fail fast across many apps.
topics.sampleQuestion: How built out should my v1 be before I launch it?

topics.label: Onboarding and the first session
topics.summary: One-step onboarding, one action per screen, and an aha moment in under 60 seconds.
topics.sampleQuestion: What should a new user experience in the first minute of my app?

topics.label: UGC seeding and creative testing
topics.summary: Small CPM-paid creators seed the first users; winning formats get scaled as paid with variations.
topics.sampleQuestion: How should I spend my first $20K a month on marketing a consumer app?

topics.label: Finding app ideas
topics.summary: Reboot proven behavior with a better flow and a new distribution channel, tied to a strong human desire.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I find a consumer app idea that has a real shot at going viral?

topics.label: Pricing and monetization
topics.summary: Low weekly subscriptions priced by regional GDP, pay-or-share gates, and no hard paywalls.
topics.sampleQuestion: Should my consumer app use a hard paywall or weekly pricing?

principles.text: Put sharing inside the core action so person A brings person B; pre-PMF, get 90%+ of users through the share loop.
Ship a bare-minimum v1 fast, then iterate with small measured tweaks: keep the wins, roll back the losses.
Use UGC only to seed the first 1K users; the viral loop has to carry the next 1M.
Find behavior people already do online that is poorly optimized, then give it a faster flow and a new distribution channel.
Give users a magic moment in under 60 seconds: one-step onboarding and one central action per screen.

sampleQA.question: How should I spend a small marketing budget on a new consumer app?

answer.text: With around $20K a month, test a dozen creatives instead of betting it all on one, and pair them with an invite loop.
Use small UGC creators paid on a CPM basis, find the winning format, then run it as ads or variations on fresh accounts.
Treat UGC as seeding only: get 1,000 to 10,000 users, then let the loop bring the rest so you are not re-buying users.

sampleQA.question: How should I price and monetize a consumer app?

answer.text: Sell weekly subscriptions priced by each country's GDP per capita so it is always a low impulse buy.
Avoid hard paywalls; let users feel the value first instead of turning away 95% of them at the door.
Offer a pay-or-share gate, like 99 cents or share on Snapchat, which drove many organic NGL downloads.

sampleQA.question: What makes a viral loop actually work?

answer.text: The first exposure should be a friend's post, so social proof is built in before the user even opens the app.
Deliver the aha moment first, then ask for the share in a way that fits the context.
Sharing must not make the sharer look lame; it should feel like a socially acceptable endorsement.
Every loop needs a clear expectation, a simple action, and an obvious reward.
